gen-dafont-existence-gf-ovo: Chunky, porthole-eyed letters up top, then a text serif below whose thins barely dip under its thicks. And a full page of Ovo would read in a dignified, spacious way, with short ascenders keeping the lines tight.
gen-dafont-existence-manrope: Existence stamps out industrial headings where every part carries the same visual mass, counters wide like glass portholes. And Manrope carries a longer read gently, its curves opening bright and its pen line holding one width throughout.
gen-dafont-existence-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and friendly, its e never squeezed shut. A long stretch of it moves smoothly, every stroke cut to one width, while Existence sits above in its blunt industrial porthole shapes.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-domine: Domine brings compact ascenders and a slight pinch where curves meet stems, giving a dignified serif voice. Shrink Franchise, though, and its jammed-together outline letters would lose their punch, while the body keeps its breathing room.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-esteban: Spaghetti-like strokes of one width define Franchise, tall and tightly packed. Esteban, by contrast, is the one for sustained reading, its serif bowls thinning gracefully and its lowercase running large beside the capitals.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-faustina: Authoritative is the mood here, with Franchise running strokes that never swell or thin. Faustina, a text serif with pliers-like open c shapes, is the one built to hold a body of words together.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-halant: Franchise draws tall, tightly packed letters with a marker-nib line that ignores direction. Make it small, though, and Halant's towering x-height and faint thick-thin shift would take over the page.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-hedvig-letters-s: Hedvig Letters Serif has open-ended curves and a sturdy, tall lowercase with moderate contrast. And Franchise, bent-paperclip strokes crammed together, gives it a punchy counterweight that makes the softer serif feel even more settled.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-marcellus-sc: Dignified and literary, Marcellus SC leans on gentle modulation. Franchise, outlined in one steady thickness, hits hard in tight tall letters, and the classic serif below it swells softly in each round letter to make the strongest contrast.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab reads with sturdy downstrokes and slender turns, and its large x-height holds up nicely on a screen. Franchise, drawn like spaghetti, handles the loud top line.
